THE TALK & THINK SUBJECT

Name it, sound it, spot it again.

Talk & Think is the subject where language and little thoughts grow together: your voice names what your baby sees, animal sounds add play, and seeing the same pictures again builds early recognition. Every Talk & Think class is short, calm and designed to be led by you.

Talk & Think is the subject where language and little thoughts grow together. Long before children can answer, they recognise: the cat on the card, the cup in their hands, the sound you make when you say woof. Classes in this subject pair realistic animals, familiar objects, body parts and everyday actions with simple naming, sound play, action games and repetition, so early recognition grows at your child’s own pace. Every Talk & Think class is short, calm and designed to be led by you.

Lesson 5 · 6–9 monthsTalk & Think

Animals & Everyday Objects

Realistic animals alongside a ball, a shoe, a cup and more — name them, add the sounds, and let early recognition grow. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
Lesson 6 · 9–12 monthsTalk & Think

First Actions & Body Parts

Body parts and first actions — hand, foot, clapping, waving — say the word, do the action, and let your little copier join in. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
Lesson 7 · 12–18 monthsTalk & Think

First Words: Food & Home

Everyday foods and home things — apple, cup, spoon, bed — name them, pause, and let the first words grow. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
Lesson 8 · 18–24 monthsThink & Talk

First Concepts

Big and small, up and down, full and empty — six concept pairs in realistic pictures, ready for a short game of say it and look. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
Lesson 9 · Age 2Think & Talk

Colors and Shapes

Eight colors, seven shapes, big-button find-it games and real-world hunts — a first interactive class made for two-year-old hands. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
Lesson 10 · Age 2Think & Talk

Matching and Sorting

Same and different, big-button find-the-match games, gentle sorting and an odd-one-out finish — noticing relationships, made for two-year-old hands. Three to five playful minutes.

Start today’s class ↗
